name: security-oauth-par-binding-review
intent: Pushed Authorization Request binding to client, transaction and expiry
artifacts: PAR request/response, client authentication, request_uri storage, authorization consumer and issuer policy.
trace: Trace who creates and redeems a request_uri, which client/parameters it binds, and how replay or expiry is enforced at authorization.
experiment: Use two owned clients in an issuer fixture; compare the rightful redemption with a client-swapped or expired reference and inspect resulting authorization state.
disproof: A random request_uri error or a 403 at PAR is not an authorization bypass; a nested redirect string alone is not a redirect consumer.
repair: Bind the pushed request to the authenticated client and lifetime, then retest intended authorization and substitution denial.
branch_decisions: Check the same request_uri at creation and redemption, including authenticated client binding and lifetime. A request_uri is not an arbitrary resource URL the client should fetch. Treat repeated authorization attempts according to issuer policy/specification rather than assuming every second use is forbidden.
operational_method: Distinguish public client identification from confidential client authentication at PAR; do not require a secret for every client. Retain the authenticated/identified client, persisted parameters and request_uri at redemption. Apply the applicable one-use expectation and explicitly supported browser-reload exception rather than an unrestricted reuse policy. Compare correct client redemption, a different client and a permitted reload under the actual issuer profile.
